title: OpenAI-compat: responses-v20 connection stability and rng_seed passthrough
author: Ayesha Patel
commits: 7a4e3b2: wire responses-v20 connection handshake + conn-id header
2f9c8d1: streaming frag reassembler for toolcall chunks (order + checksum)
b3d22f4: propagate rng_seed and rng_mode through bridge -> runtime
c1e5a6b: preserve user_metadata blob on proxied streams
aa9b3e0: tests and docs for responses-v20 compat
release_notes: Add compatibility layer for Responses v20: connection-level stability improvements (handshake + conn-id), robust fragment reassembly for tool/function-call streaming, passthrough of rng_seed/rng_mode for deterministic responses, and preservation of user metadata in proxied streams.
description: Motivation: Customers are adopting the new OpenAI Responses v20 variants which include connection-level semantics and explicit rng_seed/rng_mode fields that influence determinism. The existing OpenAI compatibility bridge did not fully preserve these semantics across the bridge -> runtime boundary and occasionally dropped or reordered streaming fragments for tool calls, causing partial tool payloads and downstream JSON schema breakage. This PR introduces a focused compatibility patch to: 1) surface a connection handshake to establish a stable conn-id and expected framing for long-lived streams, 2) implement a fragment reassembly layer that handles out-of-order and duplicated chunks for tool/function-call payloads, and 3) forward rng_seed and rng_mode through the bridge into the runtime RNG subsystem so customer-specified determinism is honored end-to-end. Summary of changes (high level): - responses_v20_adapter.go: add ConnectHandshake(conn-id) path and conn-level state tracking. Handshake negotiates expected chunk framing style (chunked/frag/line) and advertises supported fallback models if the selected model doesn't support the requested rng_mode. - stream/reassembler.go: new reassembler that maintains idempotent fragment sets per message id, applies checksum validation when provided, and exposes a compact API for callers to request "assembled message" with a timeout/partial fallback. This prevents truncated tool-call JSON objects from reaching the structured output decoder. - rng/seed_forwarder.go: small interface that carries rng_seed and rng_mode from the bridge to the runtime RNG provider. When rng_seed is present we pin the runtime PRNG seed prior to token sampling to make responses reproducible for the same prompt+seed+model. - headers/propagation.go: ensure x-redwood-conn-id and x-openai-rng-seed headers are mapped to internal context keys and carried on internal requests to dedicated/private deployments. - metadata_passthrough.json fixture and e2e test: assert that an arbitrary user_metadata blob (opaque JSON) submitted with the request is preserved in the final response envelope and also logged in tracing spans for auditability. - tests: add e2e for streaming stability under simulated packet reordering and unit tests for rng seed propagation. Performance note: reassembly has a small CPU cost for bookkeeping (per-fragment map) but avoids costly downstream retries and JSON reparsing. The code includes a bounded fragment map with TTL to limit memory under noisy clients. Backwards compatibility and safety: when rng_seed is not provided we follow existing behavior (runtime-managed nondeterministic sampling). The handshake is optional — older clients will fall back to line-chunking with the same compatibility shim as before. Edge cases & decisions: - We do not attempt to replay missing fragments from clients; instead we expose a partial-message fallback that can be configured to either error (default) or return the best-effort assembled chunk. - Checksums are optional; when present we validate and drop corrupted fragments (metrics emitted). Tests and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e failure in resp_v20_streaming_test (simulated network jitter) — root cause was a 50ms ephemeral race in test harness timeouts; I increased the test harness timeout and added a jitter-tolerant assertion. Final CI: all unit and integration checks passed. Review notes: please focus review on the reassembler's concurrency model (mutexing + per-message queues) and the seed forwarding safety boundary (ensure seed isn't logged or exposed to telemetry). Backwards-incompatible risk: very low — new headers are additive and handshake is opt-in. Linear tasks: ENG-1412 implement bridge handshake; ENG-1428 add deterministic seed propagation. Related support ticket: SUP-9821 (customer reported partial toolcall payloads when using v20). Checklist: - [x] Implement connection handshake and conn-id propagation - [x] Implement fragment reassembly with checksum handling - [x] Propagate rng_seed and rng_mode to runtime - [x] Preserve user_metadata through proxy - [x] Add unit & e2e tests - [x] Update docs (docs/compat/responses_v20.md) Review conversation: "Miguel Torres: Please double-check the lock acquisition order in reassembler.go; we should avoid holding the global map lock while waiting for per-message assembly timers." "Ayesha Patel: Good catch — reordered to acquire per-message lock after map lookup; added comment and unit test that reproduces the previous deadlock pattern." "Priya Raman: Approve with nit: rename x-openai-rng-seed -> x-openai-rng-seed-bin for binary seeds? Not necessary now but flagging for future." "Evan Brooks: Verified e2e locally against a mock v20 server; left one suggestion to improve metrics names." Merge outcome: merged via squash; changelog entry added to docs/compat/responses_v20.md and release notes. CI detail (checkpoints): - go vet: pass - unit tests: pass - integration/e2e: pass (after rerun) - lint: pass Known follow-ups (not blocking): - ENG-1477: add optional server-side replay of missing fragments behind a feature flag - ENG-1492: add metrics-driven alert when fragment reassembly drop rate exceeds threshold
